pr_title: Enable zero padding with float specifier for format strings
pr_body:
Godot currently supports zero padding for integers, octals and
hexadecimals when using format strings, but not for floats.

This commit adds support for zero padding for floats, thus ensuring
consistent behavior for all types, and making Godot's format specifiers'
behavior closer to c's `printf()`.

Before:
```
print("<%07.2f>" % -0.2345) #<  -0.23>
print("<%7.2f>" % -0.2345)  #<  -0.23>
```
Now: 
```
print("<%07.2f>" % -0.2345) #<-000.23>
print("<%7.2f>" % -0.2345)  #<  -0.23>
print("<%+07.2f>" % 0.2345) #<+000.23>
```

More examples can be found in the script in the following [project](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/4723725/printing.zip), if you wish to test. The code roughly mimics that for the other cases (integer/hexadecimal), with some differences.

Closes #39237

issue_context.title: Zero padding of a float is not working in a format string
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues for potential duplicates before filing yours:	
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue	
-->

**Godot version:** 3.2.1
<!-- Specify commit hash if using non-official build. -->


**OS/device including version:** Linux 64b
<!-- Specify GPU model, drivers, and the backend (GLES2, GLES3, Vulkan) if graphics-related. -->


**Issue description:**
<!-- What happened, and what was expected. -->
`%07.2f` format string should insert zeroes as a padding, but instead inserts spaces.

**Steps to reproduce:**

```gdscript
print("<%07.2f>" % [0.123])
```

output:

```c
<   0.12>
```

comparison with C:

```c
$ cat 0.c && echo --- && gcc 0.c -o 0 && ./0
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
	printf("<%07.2f>\n", 0.123);
}

---
<0000.12>
```

<!--**Minimal reproduction project:**-->
<!-- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue. Drag and drop a zip archive to upload it. -->
comments:
You should be able to use `str(0.123).pad_zeros(7)` to achieve this. That said, we should probably change the format string behavior to match `printf` behavior.

Does the `printf` "standard" have a way to pad a number with spaces?
I can work on this, if no one else is already
@mrushyendra It seems nobody is currently working on this, so go ahead :slightly_smiling_face:
